title: Product-Group Sine-Window Source Coordinate-Marginal Dephasing and Full-Vector Subset-Sum Equivalence Obstruction

theorems.statement: For any shift h = (h_1, h_aux) in Z_q x Z_q^{n-1} and visibility v in [0, 1], averaging the product-group sine-window colour state rho_{(k_1, k_aux)}(h) over uniform auxiliary labels k_aux in Z_q^{n-1} yields effective marginal visibility v_eff(h_aux) = v * 1[h_2 == ... == h_n == 0 mod q]. Thus for all q^{n-1} - 1 non-zero auxiliary shifts h_aux != 0, bar{rho}_{k_1}(h) = I_2 / 2 is independent of h_1 and k_1.

Over K product-group samples with labels A in Z_q^{n x K} and uniform prior h in Z_q^n, the h_1 mod 2 parity density difference satisfies (rho_even^{(K)} - rho_odd^{(K)})[x, x'] = (2/2^K) v^{wt_H(x XOR x')} 1[A(x - x') == (q/2, 0, ..., 0)^T mod q]. Because |G_prod| = q^n = (2M)^n = |G_cyclic|, the universal average parity advantage bound min(1/2, ((1+v)^K - 1)/(2 q^n)) and minimum copy threshold K_min are strictly invariant between cyclic and product-group readouts.

Postselecting product-group samples with k_2 == ... == k_n == 0 mod q restores scalar h_1 phase states with visibility v and group size q, but succeeds with probability P_accept = q^{-(n-1)} = 2^{-L(n-1)} per preparation, requiring E[N_prep] = K_1 * 2^{L(n-1)} source preparations for K_1 retained samples.
